args.title: Invalidate existing bearer tokens when a password is reset
args.body:
File: src/api/auth.ts

Bearer tokens are stateless JWTs verified only by signature and expiry (see requireAuth), and setPassword does not record when a password changed or revoke tokens issued earlier. As a result, a token captured before a password reset keeps working until its own expiry. Add a passwordChangedAt (or token-version) check: store the timestamp/version on the user, include it as a claim when issuing tokens, and have requireAuth reject tokens whose claim predates the user's current value.

file: src/api/auth.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

Bearer tokens are stateless JWTs checked only for signature and expiry (requireAuth in src/api/auth.ts), and the password-reset confirm handler doesn't invalidate previously issued tokens or record a password-changed timestamp/version. Fixing this needs a way to reject tokens issued before the most recent password change (e.g. a passwordChangedAt or tokenVersion claim checked in requireAuth). Opened a draft PR with this direction; further exploit details can stay on the private security thread.
